Indian Trust Fund: Information Requested with regard to Moneys Collected at Regina by Commissioner
W.M. Graham


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, April 9, 1924.

SIR, - In connection with the examination of the revenue of the Indian Trust Fund for the fiscal year 1923 - 24, I have
to request that you furnish me with copies of any statements sent in by Mr. Graham, Indian Commissioner at Regina,
in connection with his monthly remittances to your department of moneys collected by him on account of grazing and
other leases, on account of payments on land sales, or on any other account.

Are official receipts issued by Mr. Graham for the moneys collected by him? If so, copies or counterfoils of these
reports should be sent in by him to your department and transmitted by your department to this office. If no receipts
have been issued in the past Mr. Graham should be supplied with official receipt books, and copies of every receipt



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 597-600) ===
<!-- page 597 -->
should accompany his returns.

In future these statements and receipts should accompany the monthly revenue returns sent this office.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
G. GONTHIER, A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.

<!-- page 598 -->
DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, May 13, 1924.

SIR, - In reply to your letter of the 9th instant, I beg to say that, as requested, I am sending you File No. 427063-
104XA with the monthly cash statements received from Mr. W.M. Graham, Indian Commissioner at Regina, covering
collections made on account of grazing leases, which please return to me after examination by your officials. The
Department has not received any statements from Mr. Graham in connection with land, or other sales, which have not
been sent monthly to your office. In regard to the inquiry as to whether official receipts are issued by Mr. Graham for
the moneys collected by him, I may say that Mr. Graham has not issued any such receipts, but he has now been
supplied with official receipt books, together with full instructions as to how his revenue return should be made up
monthly and forwarded to the Department with copies or counterfoil of receipts issued by him attached thereto. In
future this revenue return will take the place of the cash statements that he has been forwarding in connection with
grazing leases.


Your obedient servant,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Auditor General.

Indian Trust Fund, Revenue: Asking for List of all Leases


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, April 9, 1924.

SIR, - In connection with the examination of the revenue of the Indian Trust Fund I have to request that you furnish
me with a list of all leases of Indian land for grazing or farming or for any other purposes that were in force on
April 1st, 1923, with full particulars as to the terms of the leases, when granted, and the period for which they were
granted, together with a statement of all payments made on account of such leases up to date.

I should also like a similar statement with regard to Indian lands that have been sold and which had not been fully paid
for on April 1st, 1923.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
G. GONTHIER, A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.



NOTE. - No reply had been received to the above letter up to the time of printing.

Trust Fund Revenue: Payments for Services of Crop Inspector from Proceeds of Crop Share Leases.


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, May 20, 1924.

SIR, - According to Mr. Commissioner Graham's statements of his Grazing Leases Account, Mr. G.H. Gooderham,
agent at the Blackfoot Indian Reserve, collected $5,662.52 in the month of January, 1924, on account of crop share
leases. Of this amount be remitted $5,312.52 to Mr. Graham, the difference of $350 being paid to Mr. T. Henderson
for 31 months' services, as crop inspector from August 16th to November 30th.

<!-- page 599 -->
This procedure, in my opinion, is at variance with section 37 of the Consolidated Revenue and Audit Act, which
requires all officers to pay over the gross revenue to the account of the Receiver General. Mr. Gooderham should have
remitted to Mr. Graham, for transmission to your department, the whole

<!-- page 600 -->
amount collected by him, and after Mr. Henderson's employment had been properly authorized, a departmental cheque,
chargeable against the Blackfoot Trust fund, should have been issued in payment of his services.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.



NOTE. - No reply had been received to the above letter up to the time to printing.

Trust Fund Revenue: Information desired in connection with Leases of a Crop Share Basis


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, May 20, 1924,

SIR, - I notice from the statements of Mr. Commissioner Graham's Grazing Leases Account which were sent me
recently that a number of the leases, especially of land on the Blackfoot reserve, appear to be on a crop share basis.

I understand that in such cases the whole cost of sowing, cultivating and harvesting the crop is borne by the lessee, and
that a certain proportion of the crop reverts to your department as rental for the land occupied, to be placed to the
credit of the band of Indians to whom the land belongs.

I should be glad to have this system of crop share leases more fully described, especially along the line of the
following queries: What proportion of the crop reverts to the department? What check has the department on the
amount harvested? Is the whole crop marketed by the lessee and the department's share paid in cash, or does the
department receive its share in grain?, Is the department's share payable immediately after threshing operations are
completed, or only after all the grain has been marketed? Is any provision made in the crop leases for the carrying of
hail insurance by the lessee?


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.

NOTE. - No reply had been received to the above letter up to the time of printing.
